newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-May 2.

text.p: There are 60 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that British influence in the territory was fading, and the present British Hong Kong policy was agreed by both major parties. After the handover, the only force that could contend with Beijing would be the United States, and Washington would replace london as the main force monitoring Beijing's Hong Kong policy, the paper said.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said there might be some minor flaws in the consultation paper on proposed amendments to two civil liberties ordinances, but the consultation had helped making the amendments better. The amendments would have a positive impact on the future development of democracy and the rule of law in Hong Kong, it said.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the Hong Kong government clearly regarded the U.S. decision to put the territory back on the intellectual property rights "watch list" as a slap in the face. But there is no denying that Hong Kong has more than its fair share of unscrupulous operators, and with Washington hell bent on catching wrongdoers, companies who think they can get away with it are simply fooling themselves.
